The Exact Gradient of the Marginal Criterion

Source: R/outer_gradient.R
statmod_marginal_grad.Rd

Computes \(\partial V/\partial\eta\) at the penalized mode, over the free scale of the hyperparameters under estimation.

Usage

statmod_marginal_grad(
  spec,
  design,
  coef,
  hyper,
  method,
  idx,
  basis = NULL,
  free = TRUE,
  ctx = NULL,
  gam = NULL
)

Arguments

spec

A StatmodSpec().

design

The design.

coef

The coefficients at the penalized mode.

hyper

The hyperparameters.

method

An OuterMethod().

idx

The outer index.

basis

The integrated subspace, or NULL.

free

Whether to carry the result onto the free scale. The Hessian assembly calls this function with free = FALSE and applies its own second-order chain rule.

ctx

The evaluation context, or NULL.

gam

The coefficients that the criterion estimates, from marginal_coords(), or NULL.

Value

A numeric vector, one entry per row of idx followed by one per position of gam$where, or NULL where the determinant does not exist.

Details

The gradient is the sum of the envelope term \(-\partial\rho/\partial\theta\), the explicit derivative of the determinant, \(-\tfrac12\mathrm{tr}(M\,\partial S/\partial\theta)\), the implicit one, \(-\tfrac12 u'v\), and, where a penalty's Hessian depends on the coefficients, \(-\tfrac12\mathrm{tr}(M\,\partial S/\partial\beta[v])\). Here \(v = -J^{-1}\,\partial^2\rho/\partial\beta\partial\theta\) is how the mode moves, \(u_c = \mathrm{tr}(M\,\partial K/\partial\beta_c)\) is how the determinant reads that movement, and \(M\) is \(K^{-1}\) under reml() and the inverse of \(K\) on the integrated subspace under ml().

The matrix \(J\) is the curvature of the penalized likelihood at the mode: the observed information plus the penalty's Hessian, plus the second derivative of a block that moves with its coefficients (mode_curvature()). It differs from \(K\) when the criterion reads the expected information. A coefficient that the criterion estimates, a direction that the model does not identify and a coordinate that a kink of a break-point term holds do not move with \(\theta\), and the function solves on the directions that they leave free (mode_solver()). Where a penalty covers the parameters of a structural term, the function delegates to statmod_structural_grad().

\(u\) is assembled without forming any third-derivative array. Writing \(G_{ab,i} = x_{ia}'M_{[a][b]}x_{ib}\) for the per-observation diagonal of the block of \(M\), $$u_{k} = -X_k'\Big(w \sum_{a,b} \ell'''_{abk}\, G_{ab}\Big),$$ one crossprod per distribution parameter. The component \(\ell'''_{abk}\) is looked up by a name built from the parameter names in the family's own order, never parsed out of one.

For each coefficient in gam, which the criterion estimates, the entry is the score of the log-likelihood in that coefficient minus half of the movement of the determinant along the direction in which the mode moves when the coefficient changes by one unit.
